summary: The GW4 appearance read is what these claims are fixing. Seven of the fifteen are certain to start - Raya, Pickford, Gvardiol, Milenkovic, Haaland, Tavernier, Schade - and two are likely: Marmoush, who has started Tottenham's last two, and Garner, who started against Man Utd but came off on 77 minutes and now carries an unspecified injury at 75%. The other six are not GW4 players: Doku is out (calf, expected back 13 September, the day of the derby and a day after the deadline), Collins came off after 17 minutes with a calf strain and is at 25%, Bijol was benched at Brighton, Munoz came on at 59 minutes on his Forest debut, Barcola has 26 minutes at Liverpool, and Strand Larsen was behind Nketiah at Fulham. Nine likely starters is two short of an XI. Two changes against this morning's board. Bijol is back on it at rank 3: Leeds' own team news has him on the bench with Muharemovic and Elvedi preferred, his minutes have gone 90, 45, 29, and the model's avail 0.75 still reads him as a starter, so its +3.0 on Maguire is too small. And Doku is off it - the model's per-gameweek line for him is 0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9, 0.7 across GW4-8, which never recovers him at all, so its 2.5 is a floor rather than a forecast for a player who misses one gameweek. Justin sits fifth of six on 124 points, so his claims process second in the queue when the window closes on 11 September: rank 1 is the one nearly certain to land.

claims.why: Mitchell scored twice as Palace came from behind twice to win 3-2 at Fulham, and has started all three league games. Munoz went the other way in the same window and came on at 59 minutes for Ola Aina on his Forest debut against Tottenham - Neco Williams has played every minute at wing-back and scored 6 and 7 points doing it. Watch one thing: Ben Chilwell has re-signed for Palace and scored the winner at Fulham with his first touch after replacing Mitchell on 73 minutes.
claims.model: Model has Mitchell at next5 16.4 (avail 0.98) against Munoz at 6.4 (avail 0.34), the widest gap on the board, and Palace have the kindest run in the league by its own fixture term (+0.5), starting at home to Ipswich. Agree - but note the model is reading Munoz off 85 minutes played while his Palace exit was negotiated, so if Glasner puts the man he signed as a right wing-back specialist straight into his back three, this one ages badly.

claims.why: Barcola has 26 minutes to his name since his GBP106m move from PSG - one substitute cameo at Ipswich - and Iraola is publicly preaching patience after a disrupted pre-season, saying he is 'in a good place' rather than that he is about to start. Le Fee has played 79, 89 and 90 minutes, and scored Sunderland's equalising penalty at Brentford. This is the stash to cash: of the two midfielders sitting idle, Doku is the one due back inside the horizon.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 17.0 (avail 1.00) against Barcola at 2.3 (avail 0.16), but most of that gap is the model having zero career matches on a marquee arrival - it is a placeholder, not a judgement. Agree anyway: even generously assuming Barcola starts from GW6, Le Fee's five certain starts beat three.

claims.why: Leeds' own team news for Brighton names Bijol among the substitutes, with Nico Elvedi making a full debut alongside Tarik Muharemovic and James Justin in the back line. His minutes have gone 90, 45, 29 across the three gameweeks, which is a selection decision hardening rather than a knock. Maguire has played every minute of Manchester United's season.
claims.model: Model has Maguire at next5 15.5 (avail 1.00) against Bijol at 12.5 (avail 0.75) and calls it +3.0, which understates it - avail 0.75 still reads Bijol as a starter who missed a game, not as the fourth-choice centre-half Farke's last team sheet makes him. Overruling the size of the gap, not its direction.

claims.why: Brentford's captain was forced off after 17 minutes against Sunderland and Keith Andrews said only 'it's a calf strain, I don't know the extent'. Two days on the club has still published no scan result and no timeline, and Brentford are away at Bournemouth in GW4. Hill has played every minute for Bournemouth and faces Brentford at home in the same fixture.
claims.model: Model has Hill at next5 15.9 (avail 0.98) against Collins at 10.9 (avail 0.20). The +5.0 is honest rather than injury-inflated - the model already has Collins back and scoring normally from GW5, so this is Hill being the better defender over the run, not just the fitter one this week.

claims.why: The one to skip if you want to skip one. Garner was substituted in the 77th minute against Man Utd and now carries an unspecified injury with a 75% chance of playing, but 75% is not an absence, and he has been building back from July groin surgery at 11, 61 and 76 minutes - the trend is upward, not downward. Scott is the safer body: every minute for Bournemouth, a goal and an assist in the last two. Submit last so it only lands if the four above have.
claims.model: Model has Scott at next5 16.6 (avail 0.96) against Garner at 9.7 (avail 0.50) and puts this swap on its own board at +7.0. Partly overruling it: the 0.50 is measured off the games Garner missed recovering from surgery, so if the knock passes he is worth far more than 9.7 and this becomes a downgrade.

claims.why: Woltemade left Newcastle for Juventus on a season-long loan on deadline day, so he plays in Serie A, not the Premier League, until at least next summer - a mandatory drop, not a judgement call. Igor Jesus is confirmed as Forest's starting striker in their predicted XI for Friday's game against Tottenham.
claims.model: Model: Igor Jesus next5 14.5 vs Woltemade 0.3, +14.2. Fully agree - the loan has pushed Woltemade's number to essentially zero, the clearest drop in the squad.

claims.why: Eze is still stuck behind Arsenal's front line under Arteta with no sign of a minutes trend pointing up. Rayan is confirmed in Bournemouth's predicted attacking three alongside Kluivert and Tavernier for the Newcastle game, and is being talked up as a breakout name this season.
claims.model: Model: Rayan next5 16.2 vs Eze 8.0, +8.2. Agree with the model - Eze's bench role explains the gap and there is no sign of it closing.

sources.title: Could Bournemouth's Rayan become the Premier League's next Brazilian star?

claims.why: This is a hedge, not an urgent need. Garner's recovery from groin surgery is running ahead of schedule and he started for Everton in midweek against Preston, but Moyes still is not trusting him for a full 90 minutes. Gross is a fully fit, nailed-on Brighton starter with no fitness question at all. Only use this claim if you want the safer floor rather than Garner's upside.
claims.model: Model: Gross next5 16.0 vs Garner 10.1, +5.9. Partial overrule - the model cannot see Garner's accelerated recovery, so the real gap is probably smaller than 5.9, but Gross is nailed and Garner still is not.

runs.note: first run - four claims submitted (Munoz drop upgraded from yesterday's hold after fresh reporting on his Aina competition); a fifth was not included since the rest of the squad is either performing above its model rating (Marmoush, kept) or has no clear replacement worth the waiver priority this week

No material change since the last run 18 minutes ago. Refreshed sourcing - confirmed Igor Jesus as Forest's starting striker ahead of Chris Wood, and Bournemouth's Hill, Rayan and Tavernier all in the latest predicted XI - and confirmed Bijol is not a drop risk since his two rivals for the Leeds centre-back shirt (Rodon, Gruev) are both injured. Still no fifth claim: Marmoush's real starting role beats his model rating and the rest of the squad is performing at or above its number.

No change to the four claims after a full club-by-club refresh - the model's numbers for every add/drop pair are unchanged and every squad member's situation (Munoz vs Aina, Woltemade in Serie A, Eze benched, Garner's careful reintroduction, Bijol's injured rivals) still checks out. The one new find was a pundit piece projecting Marmoush inside Tottenham's actual strongest XI going forward, reinforcing rather than changing the decision to keep him over a fifth claim.

Dropped the Hill-for-Munoz claim: Forest's own predicted XI (published this morning) has Munoz starting at right wing-back against Spurs, not competing with Aina, so he is no longer a drop candidate and no other squad DEF clears the swap bar. Igor Jesus/Woltemade, Rayan/Eze and Gross/Garner carried forward unchanged after a full club-by-club refresh; also checked Barcola (now live in the pool, possible bench debut Friday at Ipswich) but no squad MID is weak enough to justify dropping for him.

First run for the GW4 window (GW3 waivers have processed and the squad moved on since last week's file, which is now filed under previous). Four claims: Igor Jesus for Marmoush (Forest's confirmed #1 striker over Wood vs a Marmoush facing real competition from Solanke), Ampadu for Garner (Garner was a sub, not a starter, at Preston as earlier reported, and is behind Hackney for Sunday), Le Fee for Barcola (Barcola confirmed bench for his Liverpool debut), and a low-confidence Rayan for Doku (Doku's return is pegged for right around this gameweek, so it's a hedge). No fifth claim - the rest of the defense and attack are confirmed starters outperforming their model numbers.

No change. Re-checked all four adds and drops (Igor Jesus/Marmoush, Ampadu/Garner, Le Fee/Barcola, Rayan/Doku) plus rivals across a fresh club-by-club sweep 13 minutes after the last update - Forest's Munoz/Milenkovic, Rodon's hamstring, Doku's calf timeline and Barcola's expected bench debut at Ipswich all check out exactly as before. Still no fifth claim; the rest of the squad remains confirmed starters above their model numbers.

Dropped Ampadu for Garner: Garner is now confirmed set to start against Man Utd (Hackney a doubt with a knock), reversing last night's bench read, and no other squad midfielder or defender is weak enough once confirmed starting roles are accounted for. Kept Igor Jesus/Marmoush (reworded - Solanke's ankle injury has actually improved Marmoush's own case, so this is now a value upgrade not a bench-risk swap) and Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku unchanged. Three claims this week, down from four.

Also upgraded Rayan/Doku from low to medium confidence: Doku's calf return now points to around 13 September, which is after GW4's own deadline (12 September), so this is no longer just a timing hedge. No change to which three claims are made.

No change. Fresh club-by-club sweep ~8 hours later re-confirmed all three claims (Igor Jesus/Marmoush, Le Fee/Barcola, Rayan/Doku) plus checked Bijol, Garner and the rest of the squad for anything that would open a fourth claim - nothing did. Reports naming Aina ahead of Munoz at Forest right wing-back surfaced but only through unpermitted outlets, so Munoz was not added as a drop candidate on that alone.

Reordered rather than changed: Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku swap to ranks 1-2 (Barcola still bench-bound for today's Ipswich debut, Doku still out for today's Coventry game) and Igor Jesus/Marmoush drops to rank 3 at low confidence, since Marmoush is now a confirmed Tottenham starter alongside Igor Jesus at Forest, leaving this as a pure model-number swap rather than a bench-risk case. Also confirmed via Palace's own site that Mateta is out three weeks with a hamstring injury, which secures Strand Larsen's role further but does not open a fourth claim since he is already kept, not dropped. Full round of GW3 matches produced real news the model can't see: Igor Jesus was not even in Forest's 18 today (Delap started, Wood the sub), killing the Igor Jesus/Marmoush claim outright since Marmoush started and played 84 minutes for Spurs - dropped rather than replaced, since Marmoush is now clearly the stronger, more secure player of the two. In its place, two fresh DEF claims from today's confirmed lineups: Bijol was benched for the first time this season at Leeds (Elvedi/Muharemovic started), and Munoz was again only an impact sub at Forest, reinforcing his existing low model rating - both sourced directly off Sky Sports lineup pages rather than predicted-XI aggregators. A fifth, low-confidence claim was added on the back of Nathan Collins' calf strain (forced off after 17 minutes for Brentford, severity unknown) as a hedge, since the model does not yet reflect it at all. Le Fee/Barcola and Rayan/Doku carried forward with fresh sourcing (Le Fee's penalty and man-of-the-match display, Doku confirmed absent from City's 18 vs Coventry) and Le Fee/Barcola upgraded to high confidence given how comprehensively Barcola remains unintegrated.

Collins and Munoz themselves unchanged: still no Brentford timeline, still an impact sub at Forest, with no fresh GW3 fixtures for either club since Friday/Saturday's already-published results.

Dropped the Gross/Doku claim: the model's per-gameweek line for Doku is 0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9, 0.7 over GW4-8, i.e. it never recovers him at all, so its next5 of 2.5 is a floor rather than a forecast for a player the API expects back on 13 September - he misses one gameweek. Full club-by-club sweep found nothing that moves any of the five: Collins' calf still has no confirmed timeline from Brentford's own site, Bijol has had no fresh Leeds team news since last week's Brighton bench call, and Munoz remains an impact sub for Forest rather than a confirmed starter (fantasy-site chatter that he is now nailed on did not clear a permitted source, so it changes nothing here). Maresca said today only that City are 'not sure yet' whether Doku is back for the 13 September derby - restates the existing doubt without changing it, since that fixture falls after GW4's own deadline either way. Also checked Le Fee, Barcola, Strand Larsen, Maguire (took a bloody nose against Everton but played on, no fitness concern) and Scott/Hill at Bournemouth - all confirmed exactly as already priced into this file.
